tagline: Wednesday nights at Happy Valley, Sundays at Sha Tin, and the world's richest betting pools.
why: Horse racing is Hong Kong's great shared pastime. The Hong Kong Jockey Club runs some of the best-attended, highest-quality and richest racing in the world, and its betting turnover is enormous. Even people who never bet know the big horses, and an evening at Happy Valley is a classic social night out. Knowing the basics lets you join in at work, at dim sum, and at the track.

essentials.title: The Jockey Club runs everything
essentials.body: The HKJC is a non-profit that holds the legal monopoly on racing, football and lottery betting. It's one of the city's biggest taxpayers and charity donors.

essentials.title: Two racecourses
essentials.body: Happy Valley is the floodlit city-centre track, raced on Wednesday nights. Sha Tin is the big modern course in the New Territories, used mainly on weekends and for international races.

essentials.title: The season
essentials.body: Racing runs from September to July, with a summer break. There are about 88 race meetings a year.

essentials.title: Ratings and handicaps
essentials.body: Horses get a rating, and better horses carry more weight to even out races. Horses move between classes (Class 1 is the best, Class 5 the lowest).

essentials.title: Trainers and jockeys are stars
essentials.body: Only about two dozen licensed trainers and a small group of world-class jockeys compete, so the same names come up every week.

essentials.title: Hong Kong horses are world class
essentials.body: Hong Kong-trained horses regularly win abroad, and the December international races at Sha Tin attract the world's best.

essentials.title: Betting types
essentials.body: Win, Place and Quinella (first two in any order) are the basics. Exotic bets like the Triple Trio can pay millions.

names.name: Hong Kong Jockey Club
names.what: The club that runs racing and betting, founded in 1884.

names.name: Golden Sixty
names.what: Hong Kong's most beloved horse, a superstar miler who won multiple Hong Kong Horse of the Year titles. Retired in 2024.

names.name: Romantic Warrior
names.what: Champion middle-distance horse who won three Hong Kong Cups and the Cox Plate in Australia.

names.name: Ka Ying Rising
names.what: A world-beating sprinter on a long unbeaten run who won Sydney's The Everest in 2025.

names.name: Zac Purton
names.what: Australian jockey who holds the record for most wins in Hong Kong history.

names.name: Joao Moreira
names.what: Brazilian 'Magic Man', a fan-favourite jockey who set records here.

names.name: James McDonald
names.what: Australia's top jockey and Romantic Warrior's regular rider.

names.name: John Size
names.what: Legendary trainer with many trainer championships.

names.name: David Hayes
names.what: Australian trainer of Ka Ying Rising, back in Hong Kong after an earlier stint.

names.name: Silent Witness
names.what: The 2000s sprinter who won 17 races in a row, a Hong Kong legend.

names.name: Beauty Generation
names.what: Champion miler of the late 2010s, Golden Sixty's predecessor.

names.name: Happy Valley
names.what: The racecourse surrounded by skyscrapers. Its Wednesday night meetings are a tourist favourite.

timeline.event: The Hong Kong Jockey Club is founded.
Sha Tin racecourse opens on reclaimed land.
Hong Kong International Races begin, putting the city on the world map.
Football betting through the HKJC is legalised.
Romantic Warrior wins the Cox Plate in Melbourne.
Ka Ying Rising wins The Everest in Sydney, the world's richest turf sprint.

now.headline: Ka Ying Rising mania
now.detail: The sprinter's winning streak is the biggest story in local racing.

now.headline: Romantic Warrior abroad
now.detail: Its overseas trips to Australia, Dubai and Japan make it a national hero.

now.headline: The Conghua centre
now.detail: The Jockey Club's big training centre in Guangdong lets horses train in the mainland and enables racing in the Greater Bay Area.

now.headline: Young people and racing
now.detail: The HKJC is trying to bring in younger fans with themed nights at Happy Valley.

local.headline: Happy Valley Wednesdays
local.detail: Entry is cheap, the beer garden is busy, and it's a classic after-work night out with colleagues or visitors.

local.headline: Office tips
local.detail: Colleagues share tips and form guides; ask who someone fancies this Sunday.

local.headline: Jockey Club charity
local.detail: Its Charities Trust funds hospitals, parks and the arts, which is why the logo is everywhere.

local.headline: Off-course betting
local.detail: HKJC branches across the city and its app handle most betting.

debates.question: Golden Sixty or Romantic Warrior?
debates.sides: Golden Sixty's dominance at a mile versus Romantic Warrior's international wins.

debates.question: Does the betting culture cause harm?
debates.sides: Racing brings jobs and charity money, but problem gambling is a real concern.

debates.question: Should Hong Kong horses travel more?
debates.sides: Overseas wins boost prestige but risk the horses' local campaigns.
